record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.context_brief: Initial-state model selection and data constraints
record.original_question: In relativistic heavy-ion collisions that aim to create and characterize a quark-gluon plasma, what is the best model for the fluctuating initial state, and what constraints can existing flow and particle-correlation data already place on that model?

evidence.quote:
Specific questions that were addressed during this workshop include:
• What is the best model for the initial state? What constraints can we already put
on it from new data?

there is not a
binary choice between two well understood competing models for the initial condition
(e.g., ’Glauber’ versus ’CGC’), as is sometimes inferred by those not directly involved
in this research, but instead there exists a large space of possible physical pictures,
parameters, and implementations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultrarelativistic nucleus–nucleus collisions that produce a deconfined quark–gluon plasma, the early-time energy/entropy density profile in the transverse plane fluctuates event-by-event. A typical modeling pipeline assigns to each collision event an initial density ε(x,y) (drawn from a chosen "initial-state model" such as a Glauber-type wounded-nucleon or binary-collision construction, a Color Glass Condensate / IP-Glasma description, EKRT, KLN, or related variants, each with its own parameters: nucleon size, sub-nucleonic structure, color-charge fluctuations, saturation scale, etc.), evolves it via relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with transport coefficients (η/s, ζ/s) and a hadronization prescription, and computes hadronic observables.

Among such observables one has the anisotropic flow coefficients v_n and their event-by-event distributions, defined from the azimuthal Fourier expansion dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos(n(φ − Ψ_n)), together with multiparticle cumulants v_n{2k}, symmetric cumulants SC(m,n), event-plane correlations 〈cos(k_1 Ψ_{n_1}+…)〉, and various two-particle and longitudinal correlation functions, all measured as functions of centrality, collision energy, and system size.

Problem. Identify the initial-state model (specifying its functional form for ε(x,y), its fluctuation content, and its parameters) that, when coupled to a standard viscous hydrodynamic + hadronic-cascade evolution, best reproduces the full set of currently available flow and particle-correlation measurements in heavy-ion collisions. Equivalently: determine the sharpest quantitative constraints that the existing flow and correlation data place on the space of admissible initial-state models, including bounds on their key parameters (e.g., nucleon width, sub-nucleonic hot-spot structure, saturation scale, normalization, granularity) and on the geometry/eccentricity distributions ε_n that any acceptable initial-state model must produce.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of identifying the "best" fluctuating initial-state model and the constraints data place on it remains an active research area. Recent works (IP-Glasma, TRENTo Bayesian analyses, EKRT, and 2024–2025 studies on sub-nucleonic structure and short-range nucleon correlations) continue to refine, rather than settle, the model space; no consensus single best model has been established, though Bayesian inference has narrowed parameter ranges.

status_evidence.title: Imaging the initial condition of heavy-ion collisions and nuclear structure across the nuclide chart
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ongoing efforts to constrain initial conditions across systems; emphasizes that multiple complementary models and observables are needed.
status_evidence.claim: The initial state remains characterized by a family of competing models constrained jointly by flow and correlation observables.

status_evidence.title: Unmasking short-range correlations via initial-state fluctuations in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order fluctuations of the initial transverse size show >10% sensitivity to nucleon-nucleon short-range correlations.
status_evidence.claim: New observables in 2025 are still being proposed to further constrain initial-state fluctuation models.

status_evidence.title: Fluctuating Glasma initial conditions and flow in heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: IP-Glasma combines IP-Sat with classical Yang-Mills evolution including color-charge fluctuations.
status_evidence.claim: IP-Glasma is a leading candidate model but coexists with Glauber-type and EKRT alternatives.
